security.evidence: Every new write authorizes via Gate/policy before writing (CreateQueue.php:19, UpdateQueue.php:23, SetQueueAccess.php:27); call paths authorize after locking and the inactive check (CallNextTicket.php:32, Ticket.php:100-106), and the policy denies non-employees and corrupted non-array permissions (QueuePolicy.php:68-69); input is validated server-side (SetQueueAccess.php:37-50) and mass assignment is guarded (QueueAccess.php:12). No output/escaping or secret handling is involved, and authorization failures fail closed.

tests.evidence: The diff adds no tests at all: the 15 changed files are app code, factory, migration and docs (change.diff:1-704); there is no tests/ path anywhere in the diff, so none of the queue lifecycle, access-grant, policy or call-authorization requirements (including unauthorized-call cases) is covered.

simplicity.evidence: The actions are direct and reuse rules/Str (CreateQueue.php:21-36), but the same 11-line isUniqueViolation helper is copy-pasted in CreateQueue.php:56-65 and UpdateQueue.php:78-88, and QueueAccessFactory.php:36-52 adds an afterMaking hook that rewrites a membership's entity_id, which is more machinery than deriving the queue from the membership.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods focused (QueuePolicy.php:17-78, SetQueueAccess.php:58-79); the only rough spots are the SQLSTATE/message sniffing in CreateQueue.php:56-65 (magic '23000'/'UNIQUE'/'Duplicate') and the non-obvious side effect documented by a comment in QueueAccessFactory.php:49-51.

scope.evidence: All edits serve the task: actions, enum, model, factory, migration, policy, two call paths, and the requested docs (change.diff:1-704); no unrelated refactors or out-of-scope UI/delete features.

issues.explanation: No Pest/PHPUnit tests ship with this authorization-heavy change, violating the project's TDD rule and leaving queue lifecycle, grant/revoke, policy and both call paths (including unauthorized-call behavior) unverified.
isUniqueViolation returns true for any SQLSTATE '23000', so an unrelated integrity failure (e.g. a foreign-key error) is surfaced as a slug-duplicate ValidationException instead of the real error.

The policy compares $membership->role strictly against UserRole enum cases and calls User::membershipFor(), neither of which is visible in the diff (EntityMembership's shown code only uses UserRole::Owner->value in a scope); if role is not cast to UserRole, managers would always be denied call/update/manageAccess.
The identical isUniqueViolation helper is duplicated in both actions and should live in one shared place or be folded into the existing exception handling.

The afterMaking hook moves an already supplied membership to the queue's entity by saving entity_id, which can silently relocate a membership (and break the one-owner-per-entity invariant); deriving the default queue from the membership is enough.
The public __invoke methods lack the PHPDoc the conventions require on public methods touched, while QueuePolicy documents its abilities.

review.summary: The change implements the queue lifecycle actions, the queue_access table/model/enum/factory, the QueuePolicy and the authorization of both call paths, and updates the three requested docs. The implementation covers the contract and validates/authorizes correctly, but it ships with no tests at all in a TDD-mandated, security-sensitive slice, plus some duplicated exception handling and an unverified dependency on User::membershipFor()/role casting. Approve after tests are added and the minor issues are addressed.
